text: Simon Petrus, Jesu Christi servus et apostolus, iis, qui parem nostrae fidem per Dei nostri, et Servatoris Jesu Christi justitiam sortiti sunt,
note: *Servātōris* capital, Christ the Saviour (σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ; decisions 20 and 45, *Servātor* capital everywhere), as 2:20, 3:2 and 3:18 in the draft; *sunt,* with 1573's comma (*iuſtitiam ſortiti ſunt,*, canvas 922) for the draft's full stop: the sentence runs on to 1:2 *grātiam et pācem … dīcit*, as 1 Pet 1:1–2 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: gratiam et pacem plurimam dicit, in Dei et Jesu Domini nostri cognitione:
note: *grātiam* lower case, the sentence of 1:1 running on (1573 *2 gratiam*); the BSB's break not taken, as at 1 Pet 1:2 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Ita enim vobis large suppetet aditus ad aeternum Domini nostri Servatorisque Jesu Christi regnum.
note: *Servātōrisque* capital (decisions 20 and 45), as 3:18's *Dominī nostrī Servātōrisque* in the draft (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Itaque non negligam vos semper de his commonefacere, quamquam gnaros, et in praesenti veritate fixos.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:11 closes the exhortation to virtue with the entry into the kingdom, and *Itaque nōn neglegam vōs … commonefacere* opens Peter's reminder before his death (1:12–15); the BSB's breaks at 1:5 and 1:10 left (*Vōs vērō in hoc …* and *Proinde* run on the same argument) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: quippe qui a Deo Patre honorem acceperit et gloriam, voce delata ad eum hujusmodi a magnifica gloria.
note: *Deō Patre* capital, God the Father (παρὰ θεοῦ πατρός; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Hanc nos vocem audivimus de caelo delatam, quum una cum eo essemus in sacro monte: “Hic est meus carissimus Filius, in quo me oblecto.”
note: the Father's voice in “…” after *in sacrō monte:*, where 1573 prints the words (stage 2, section 2c), as the BSB's quotation in 1:17; not \\qt, the words being the gospel's, not the Old Testament's (as your Matt 17:5, *“Hic est meus cārissimus Fīlius …”*); *Hic* capital as 1573 (*monte : Hic eſt*); *Fīlius* capital, the Son (decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Adde, quod habemus firmiorem fatidicum sermonem, in quem recte facitis quod estis intenti, tamquam in lucentem in obscuro loco lucernam, donec dies illucescat, et lucifer oriatur in cordibus vestris:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Adde, quod habēmus firmiōrem fātidicum sermōnem* turns from the apostles' eyewitness to the prophets' word (1:19–21) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Non enim hominis voluntate editum est umquam oraculum, sed Sancti Spiritus instinctu locuti sunt homines divini.
note: *Sānctī Spīritūs* both capital, the Holy Spirit (ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου; decision 20), as your settled *Spīritū Sānctō*; the draft had *sānctī* lower (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Nam si Deus angelis, qui peccaverant, non pepercit, quin eos in tartarearum tenebrarum catenas praecipitatos conjecit, ad judicium custodiendos:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:3 closes the description of the false teachers with their sure ruin, and *Nam sī Deus angelīs … nōn pepercit* opens the examples of judgment (2:4–10a), the conditional sentence Castellio's annotation calls unfinished (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: At isti, similes animalibus rationis expertibus, naturaliter in praedam interitumque natis, de eis, quae ignorant, maledicunt, in sua corruptela perituri,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *At istī* turns from the angels' restraint (2:11) to the false teachers' character (2:12–16); the BSB's breaks at 2:10, 2:15, 2:17 and 2:20 left, each running on (*maximē quī*, *quī relictā*, *Iī sunt*, *Sī enim*) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Eisque accidit, quod est in illo vero proverbio: “Canis ad suum vomitum regressus, et lota sus ad caeni volutabrum.”
note: the proverb in “…” after *in illō vērō prōverbiō:*, as the BSB; one quotation, as Castellio joins the two members in one sentence (the BSB has two); not \\qt: Peter cites it as a proverb, and only its first member is Scripture (Prov 26:11) (uncertain); *Canis* capital as the quotation's first word, as 1573 (*prouerbio : Ca-/nis*, canvas 923) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Qui dicant: “Ubi est ejus promissus adventus? Nam ex quo majores obdormiverunt, omnia eodem in statu manent ab orbe condito.”
note: the scoffers' words in “…” after *Quī dīcant:*, as the BSB; *Ubi* capital as 1573 (*dicant : Vbi*, canvas 924), *Nam* after the question mark (1573 *aduentus. nam*, lower) (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Veniet autem Domini dies ut fur noctu, in qua caeli perniciter interibunt, elementa ardentia dissolventur, et tellus, et quae sunt in ea res, conflagrabunt.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Veniet autem Dominī diēs* turns from the Lord's patience (3:8–9) to the day itself (3:10–13); the BSB's break at 3:11 left, *Quod cum sint hæc omnia dissipanda* drawing the consequence of 3:10 (Claude, 2026-11-12)

text: Vos igitur, carissimi, id praecognoscentes, cavete, ne in nefariorum errorem abducti, excidatis ex vestra firmitate:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Vōs igitur, cārissimī* opens the letter's last charge and doxology (3:17–18); the BSB's breaks at 3:3, 3:5 and 3:15 left, each running on (*Hoc in prīmīs scientēs*, *Illud enim*, *Et Dominī nostrī lentitūdinem*) (Claude, 2026-11-12)
